predecessors.name: Umayyad Caliphate
predecessors.text: al-Andalus, the Iberian rump of the Umayyad realm after the Abbasid revolution (Cliopatria's last Umayyad shape equals its first Córdoba shape)

successors.name: Caliphate of Córdoba
successors.text: the same state: Abd al-Rahman III declared himself caliph 'on 16 January 929'; Cliopatria's Caliphate row begins in 936

ledger.x: 756: Abd al-Rahman I founds the Emirate of Córdoba.
757: the rest of Cliopatria's 757 al-Andalus (445,142 km2) passes to the emir from Yusuf al-Fihri's governors; no page dates any of it.
759: Narbonne capitulates to the Franks.
760: Roussillon falls to the Franks.
778: 53 cells of the Ebro valley around Zaragoza enter the Frankish shape.
778: the rest of the Upper March slips away as Charlemagne invades.
ledger.cp: rebellious lords of the Upper March

ledger.x: 783: the 53 Ebro cells leave the Frankish shape again.
783: the emir's army marches on Zaragoza.
ledger.cp: rebellious lords of the Upper March

ledger.x: 785: Girona falls to the Franks.
798: Urgell and Cerdanya pass to the Franks.
801: Louis the Pious takes Barcelona.
806: the Franks take Navarre under their protection.
825: the Duero fringe leaves the shape as Asturias begins to resettle it.
852: Toledo rises again.
859: truce with Toledo.
868: Porto falls to Asturias.
872: Furtun ibn Musa occupies Tudela.
January 872: the sons of Musa ibn Musa take Zaragoza and Monzón.
878: Viseu and Lamego are resettled by Asturias.
879: Coimbra falls to Alfonso III.
883: Umar ibn Hafsun leads the rebel south.
884: the emir takes Zaragoza.
898: the Banu Qasi submit for Tudela and Tarazona.

c. 900: the emir's power shrinks to Córdoba. 'The power of emir Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Umawi (c. 900) did not extend beyond Córdoba itself'; at his death in 912 it did not extend 'not far beyond the vicinity of Córdoba' (Abd…
903: the Balearic Islands are taken.
913: Écija and Seville return.
914: the rebel coast falls.
915: Valencia submits.
921: Guadix, Jerez and Cádiz submit.
ledger.cp: Banu Muhallab of Guadix and the lords of Jerez and Cádiz

ledger.x: 922: Pechina submits; Umayyad power is restored 'throughout al-Andalus' except Toledo, Badajoz and the Upper March.

924: the Banu Qasi are removed from Tudela. the Banu Qasi page: 'on his return to Tudela he removed the Banu Qasi and sent them to Córdoba' (the year after the fall of Viguera and Nájera in 923); the Tujibids take their place; 'The death of Muhammad ibn Lubb' in 929 ended them in the Ebro valley.
928: Bobastro surrenders.
929: Abd al-Rahman III proclaims the Caliphate of Córdoba.

wars.name: Frankish conquest of Septimania
wars.outcome: Pepin the Short's expedition of 752 ends with the capitulation of Narbonne in 759 and the taking of Roussillon in 760; the Emirate keeps nothing north of the Pyrenees.

wars.name: Abd al-Rahman I against Yusuf al-Fihri
wars.outcome: Abd al-Rahman beat Yusuf al-Fihri at al-Musarah 'just outside Córdoba in March 756'; Yusuf fled towards Toledo and died there, 759 in the infobox (one account: killed two or three years after the battle by his own men).

wars.name: Abbasid expedition to al-Andalus
wars.outcome: Al-Ala ibn Mughith's Abbasid army is defeated at Carmona: 'By 763 Abd al-Rahman had to get back to the business of war.'

wars.name: Charlemagne's Spanish expedition
wars.outcome: Invited by rebellious Muslim lords, Charlemagne failed before Zaragoza and his rearguard 'led by Roland was attacked by the Basque tribes' (Roncevaux, 15 August 778).

wars.name: Frankish conquest of the Spanish March
wars.outcome: The Franks take Girona (785), Urgell and Cerdanya (798) and Barcelona (801); the Emirate's Pyrenean frontier falls back to the Llobregat and the Ebro.

wars.name: Battle of Pancorbo
wars.outcome: A Moorish victory over the Franks in 816 (Spanish March page); no border moved.

wars.name: Banu Qasi revolts and the Upper March
wars.outcome: Musa ibn Musa revolts with Íñigo Arista in the 840s; 859 Ordoño I and García Íñiguez defeat him; the emir takes Zaragoza in 884; Lubb submits in 898; Abd al-Rahman III removes the Banu Qasi from Tudela in 924.

wars.name: Revolt of Toledo
wars.outcome: A new revolt broke out in Toledo in 852; Muhammad I's army was defeated in the reprisal; Toledo allied with Ordoño I of Asturias and lost at the Battle of Guadacelete; in 859 Muhammad I negotiated a truce.

wars.name: Asturian-Cordoban war of Alfonso III
wars.outcome: 'Fighting occurred almost constantly between 875 and 883'; Asturias gains the land between the Douro and the Mondego; peace in 884.

wars.name: Revolt of Umar ibn Hafsun
wars.outcome: The rebellion holds the south from 883; Ibn Hafsun is beaten near Polei in 891 (but 'reconquered all the lost territories' by 892), converts to Christianity in 899, makes peace in 911, dies in 917; Abd al-Rahman III takes the coast in 914 and Bobastro in 928.

wars.name: Reconquest of al-Andalus by Abd al-Rahman III
wars.outcome: Écija and Seville (913), the coast to Algeciras (914), Valencia (915), Guadix, Jerez and Cádiz (921) and Pechina (922) return; Badajoz (930), Toledo (932) and Zaragoza (937) come after the emirate.

wars.name: Campaigns of 920 and 924 against León and Pamplona
wars.outcome: In 920 Abd al-Rahman III 'captured the forts of Osma and San Esteban de Gormaz' (the page does not say whether they were garrisoned or kept, nor that León retook them), beat Navarre and León at Valdejunquera on 26 July and sacked Pamplona; in 924 he…

certainty.note: No treaty line is recorded in the pages opened: the Pyrenean frontier of the Spanish March, the Duero belt and the Upper March are approximate; from c.
